newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, eyes on stocks, strikes.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, eyes on stocks, strikes.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly weaker in modest volume Tuesday as tags stuck to a narrow range, but the backwardation on LME still see-sawed lower during the session, belying strong demand, traders said.
July COMEX settled 0.65 cent weaker at 109.55 cents per pound, traded 110.80 to 109.20 cents. Spot May went out 1.05 cents lower at 110.55 cents.
The cash-to-three months backwardation on LME was $75/$80, down from a high of $90 but off the low of $60/$65.
Brokers were paying close attention to physical metal, with some expecting an influx of copper into LME depots following the surge last week in the backwardation which peaked around $200.
Expectation of higher LME stocks and already high COMEX inventories prompted some dealers to liquidate, brokers said.
But any influx of metal onto LME, most probably in Germany, would not be significant, and would be offset by growing tightness in Europe, Fred Demler of E D and F Man International said.

"There is a real concern about what's happening in Europe right now. The Russian shipments are being delayed because of flooding, and there is a lot of swapping metal out of Europe by the major producers into the U.S. because of very strong demand in the U.S.," Demler said. "Some of the tightness that we have seen in the U.S. may soon pinch Europe."
The market also awaited developments in Chile where the Escondida strike continued, and where workers at Quebrada Blanca mine voted Sunday to strike from Wednesday.
